title: Amasya: Pontic Rock Tombs & Yeşilırmak Riverfront Guide
seoTitle: Amasya Turkey Guide: Pontic Tombs & Yeşilırmak Mansions
metaDescription: Visit Amasya via Merzifon Airport (MZH), see the Pontic King Rock Tombs illuminated at dusk, and pick the best Yalıboyu Ottoman mansion hotels.
quickAnswer: Amasya sits in a dramatic northern Anatolian river gorge, reached in 90 minutes from Istanbul via [Amasya Merzifon Airport (MZH)](https://www.flightconnections.com/flights-from-amasya-mzh) plus a 45-minute drive. Stay two nights in a restored Yalıboyu Ottoman mansion along the Yeşilırmak, walk up to the Hellenistic Pontic King Rock Tombs before sunset, and watch the cliffside tombs light up at dusk.

body.text: Few Turkish towns pack 2,300 years of royal history into one walkable river bend like Amasya. Ancient Amaseia served as the capital of the Hellenistic Kingdom of Pontus, birthplace of geographer Strabo, and the Ottoman training ground where twelve crown princes governed before seven ascended the throne ([UNESCO Tentative List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6039/)).
How do you reach Amasya by flight (Merzifon) or road?

The fastest way to reach Amasya is a direct 80-to-90-minute domestic flight from Istanbul (IST or SAW) to [Amasya Merzifon Airport (MZH)](https://www.flightconnections.com/flights-from-amasya-mzh), followed by a 45-minute transfer across the 42–47 km highway into town ([Pegasus Airlines](https://www.flypgs.com/en/airports/amasya-merzifon-airport)). By road, Amasya sits four hours northeast of Ankara and roughly 3.5 hours north of Cappadocia via Hattusa.

body.text: Pre-arrange your MZH airport car if arriving on an evening flight, as small-terminal taxi supply thins quickly. Drivers coming from Ankara or Cappadocia should pair the drive with a two-hour stop at Hattusa along the inland corridor.
Why are the Pontic King Rock Tombs best seen at dusk?

Carved directly into the sheer 272-meter limestone face of [Mount Harşena](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6039/), the five monumental Pontic King Rock Tombs catch warm late-afternoon light before floodlights switch on at twilight. Visiting the cliffside path around 16:30 and descending to the south bank of the Yeşilırmak by blue hour gives you both close-up stonework and Amasya's signature night reflection.

Built between the third and second centuries BCE for the Mithridatic kings of Pontus, the tombs rise above the Maiden's Palace terrace and rank among Anatolia's largest rock-cut royal graves ([UNESCO](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6039/)). Stone stairs lead right into carved passages behind the façades. Once you cross back over Alçak Bridge at twilight, golden floodlights against dark limestone mirror cleanly across the Yeşilırmak River.
Where are the best riverside Ottoman mansion hotels?

The finest places to stay in Amasya are the restored 19th-century timber-and-mudbrick Yalıboyu mansions (konaklar) lining Hazeranlar Sokak in the historic Hatuniye district on the north bank. Booking a river-facing room here puts you directly beneath the Pontic tombs, steps from pedestrian footbridges, and away from main-road traffic.
Check three practical details before booking any Hatuniye konak:

items: Riverfront vs. alley wing: Confirm a direct Yeşilırmak view rather than a lower-priced room facing a retaining wall.
Stairs and floorboards: Historic timber mansions lack elevators and carry footsteps; light sleepers should request an upper corner room.
Luggage drop-off: Hazeranlar Sokak is narrow and pedestrianized, so confirm driver drop-off at Alçak Bridge.

body.text: How many nights does Amasya deserve?

Amasya deserves two nights (roughly 36 to 48 hours)—enough time to absorb two evening illuminations along the river without running out of sights. One night feels rushed once you factor in airport transfers, while three nights only make sense if you plan day trips to Boraboy Lake or Merzifon's historic mosques.
A crisp two-day plan follows [GoTürkiye's 48-hour Amasya route](https://goturkiye.com/amasya/48-hours):

items: Day 1: Walk Hatuniye's riverfront, visit the 1485 Sultan Bayezid II Mosque Complex and the Sabuncuoğlu Şerefeddin Museum of Medicine (inside a 1308 Ilkhanid hospital), then climb to the Pontic Rock Tombs before sunset.

Day 2: Taxi up to Amasya Castle on Mount Harşena for gorge panoramas, tour the Amasya Archaeological Museum (famed for 14th-century Ilkhanid mummies), and eat keşkek and poppy-seed Amasya çöreği with samovar tea.

faq.q: Is Amasya easy to visit without a rental car?
faq.a: Yes. Historic Amasya is compact and walkable along both riverbanks; you only need short taxis for Amasya Castle and Merzifon Airport.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to visit Amasya?
faq.a: April–June and September–October bring 18°C–26°C days and clear skies. July and August turn hot inside the narrow gorge, while winter is crisp and occasionally snowy.

faq.q: Are the Pontic King Rock Tombs a UNESCO World Heritage Site?
faq.a: Mount Harşena and the Rock-Tombs of the Pontic Kings have been on Türkiye's [UNESCO World Heritage Tentative List](https://whc.unesco.org/en/tentativelists/6039/) since April 2015.

faq.q: What local dishes should you try in Amasya?
faq.a: Order slow-cooked keşkek, bakla dolması (fava-bean stuffed vine leaves), poppy-seed Amasya çöreği at breakfast, and crisp misket apples in autumn ([GoTürkiye](https://goturkiye.com/amasya/48-hours)).

faq.q: Can you visit Amasya as a day trip from Samsun?
faq.a: Yes, Samsun is under two hours away, but a day trip skips Amasya's signature experience: watching the floodlit tombs reflect in the river after dark.

faq.q: Do Amasya hotels and restaurants accept credit cards?
faq.a: Yes. Visa and Mastercard work widely, though small Turkish Lira notes are useful for tea gardens, bakeries, and taxis (see our [Türkiye money guide](https://itineraryofturkiye.com/blog/currency-money-in-turkey-2026)).
